newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat falls on prospect of good rain.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat falls on prospect of good rain.

text.p: The Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures fell back significantly on Wednesday as the prospect of rain in Australia's drought-stricken east and south increased.

Chicago's overnight fall on the higher estimate of U.S. wheat production by the Sparks analytical firm contributed to Wednesday's selling of SFE wheat futures, Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said.
The main influence, however, was predictions of rain in Australia's east and south, he said.

In SFE floor trades on Wednesday this spilled over into selling of the January 1998 and March 1998 contracts, down by A$3.50 a tonne each. It also produced a flurry of trades in put options on the January contract at strike prices between A$190.00 and A$200.00.
Rain in parts of South Australia, Victoria and Western Australia in the past 24 hours was expected by some to increase to general rain on Thursday and Friday, Booth said.
Some predictions were for anything up to an inch of rain in southern New South Wales (NSW) and parts of northern NSW.
"This could take the heat out of this over-bought market."
Wednesday floor trades took January 1998 and March 1998 down to A$196.50 and A$199.00 a tonne respectively on heavier than normal volume.
January 1998 also attracted heavy put option interest, with a total of 30 puts trading at strike prices of A$190.00, A$195.00 and A$200.00. Premiums were A$6.00, A$8.40 and A$12.00 respectively.
